training.validation_schedule: final optimizer update only; best is not multi-evaluation selection
training.bn_caveat: Per-rank training running statistics, not SyncBN; bridge backbone always eval.
training.scale_caveat: Each data scale uses its own same-100-update warmup; scale comparison includes warmup data exposure, not CLIP data alone.

visual_check.scope: 384 temporally sampled frames including native and historical bridge controls; not continuous audio-video human review or exact hand-quality acceptance
visual_check.observation: Motion motifs and timing differ, especially staircase turns/leg curls; red-shirt and shop retain common arm motifs. No whole-scene/identity collapse seen in the sampled thumbnails; hand detail remains uncertain.

conclusion.retrieval_learning: Scale helps lambda0 at equal updates (+3.75 percentage points), not lambda1; more updates improve both retrieval scores.
conclusion.native_interface: Neither scaling nor more updates consistently restores native acoustic representation/reconstruction.
conclusion.generation_claim: No reliable consistent advantage over native or historical bridge-only established; this is insufficient evidence of benefit, not proof that the encoder cannot control music.
conclusion.next_decision: Do not automatically expand data or sweep more recipes. Review these fixed cases, then prioritize explicitly testable choreography-control interfaces rather than claiming retrieval gain as video gain.
